source.author: verg
source.text: Ipse etiam, eximiae laudis succensus amore, Ascanius curvo direxit spicula cornu; nec dextrae erranti deus afuit, actaque multo perque uterum sonitu perque ilia venit harundo.
source.text_original: Ipse etiam, eximiae laudis succensus amore, / Ascanius curvo direxit spicula cornu; / nec dextrae erranti deus afuit, actaque multo / perque uterum sonitu perque ilia venit harundo.
source.text_english: Ascanius himself too, kindled by desire for outstanding praise, bent his curved bow and directed his shafts; nor was the god absent from his wavering hand, and the dart, driven with a loud sound, passed through the belly and through the flanks.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: ipsum etiam curisque parem talesque prementem corde metus ducit, facilem tamen, Aesona coniunx.
reuse.text_original: ipsum etiam curisque parem talesque prementem / corde metus ducit, facilem tamen, Aesona coniunx.
reuse.text_english: It also leads him to fear himself, equal to his cares and weighing down such fears in his heart, yet tractable, wife of Aeson.
